thread:
sre-oncall: Heads-up — pen test report (ticket 4567) calls out audit-log sampling that may leak KMS key IDs. Support tried a retest and hit intermittent 503s; customer saw latency spikes while running the repro. Attaching context and logs below, need triage and a clear owner.

oliver: assigning to sec-crypto for triage. @maya can you look at the CloudTrail artifacts + sampling config?

maya: looking now. quick q — is the reproduce run using our prod logging bucket or an ingest-sharded test cluster?

sre-oncall: support used prod-copy bucket snapshot & a short window query. repro steps they ran: `aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=ResourceName,AttributeValue=arn:aws:kms:...` and then grepped for key alias. sometimes CloudTrail returned partial results, hence 503s from the internal log-proxy.

support-ian: I was on the call with the customer — they ran a scan across many accounts, saw ~1.2% of events with a truncated resource field. thought it might be an ingestion-time truncate by our log-parsers.

maya: ok grabbing the raw S3 object for the timeframe. initial glance: some gzipped files include truncated JSON lines where `resource` field ends with `...` — looks like a streaming chunk boundary.

security-bot: automated note: ticket 4567 severity flagged as P2 due to potential sensitive metadata exposure. Evidence artifacts uploaded to /evidence/4567/ .

oliver: two threads here — (1) whether KMS identifiers appearing in CloudTrail are expected (they often are), and (2) whether our log-processing/rotation creates truncated lines that make leak hunting easier. need remediation plan and a retest checklist.

maya: quick mitigation idea: tighten ingestion backpressure so chunk boundaries are not emitted as partial JSON lines — patch in ingestion pipeline to buffer 8KB extra per object and validate line completeness. can test on staging.

product-lena: we should also confirm retention policy docs — legal asked which environments keep CloudTrail logs >90 days. need clear owner and customer-facing wording.

sre-oncall: agreed. priority: prevent further accidental partial-exposure, then retest the pen find. who's owning the codefix?

oliver: @maya will lead the workaround/patch. @support-ian coordinate with customer for a controlled retest window. @product-lena draft the comms. I'll handle severity review with compliance.

maya: plan: 1) reproduce truncated-lines locally with the exact streaming chunk size (I have the raw object). 2) implement buffer patch on staging ingestion, run test scan that previously yielded truncated resource fields. 3) observe whether log-proxy 503s go away. ETA ~ 24-36h.

support-ian: I'll schedule retest slot with the customer tomorrow 09:00 PT and provide the exact API calls. ask them to limit concurrency to avoid overloading the log-proxy.

sre-oncall: note — during the initial retest we also saw auth failures for the service principal used for sampling (403s). can security confirm there were no policy changes?

maya: checking IAM change log now — no policy updates in that window. 403s likely correlated with our rate-limiter rejecting signed requests when the backend returned 503. sequence: backend 503 -> retries -> signed requests expire -> 403. fix the root 503s and the auth flakiness should disappear.

oliver: good catch. we'll include that in the remediation notes.

security-bot: reminder: add unit tests to prevent regressions for streaming-parsing and include a smoke test in the deploy pipeline that replays a sampled CloudTrail object.

maya: noted. will add parser-completeness test and a small replay harness.

product-lena: compliance/comms: what's the customer-facing line? "We identified an ingestion bug that sometimes produced partial log records; we throttled ingestion and will re-run scans to validate there is no residual exposure." ok?

oliver: tweak: add timeline & mitigation steps and offer to share sanitized evidence from the retest. keep wording non-alarmist.

support-ian: customer asked for severity downgrade if retest shows no reproductions. we should predefine pass/fail criteria: no truncated resource fields and no 5xx from log-proxy across a 1-hour controlled scan.

sre-oncall: agreed. add requirement that the retest uses a separate test snapshot and our staging patch first. if pass -> we close the finding and mark as remediated; if fail -> escalate to P1 and involve infra-leads.

maya: starting patch branch now: `git checkout -b fix/ingest-buffer-4567` — I'll post PR when ready.

oliver: thanks. can someone upload minimal sanitized artifact showing truncated line sample to ticket? that's useful for postmortem.

support-ian: uploaded `trunc_sample_4567.json.gz` to evidence folder and linked in ticket.

sre-oncall: final ask: security/compliance — confirm retention defaults so we can close the compliance angle in the writeup. @oliver can you confirm?

oliver: compliance confirmed: production CloudTrail is 365 days by default for this customer tier; we'll document that and call out where staging differs.

security-bot: scheduled follow-up: retest check-in in 36 hours.

maya: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/ingest/pulls/888. patch buffers by 12KB and adds complete-line validation. running unit tests now.

support-ian: retest confirmed with customer for 09:00 PT tomorrow. I'll post results into this thread.

oliver: marking owner fields in the ticket: sec-crypto:maya, support:ian, product:lena, compliance:oliver.

sre-oncall: thanks all. we'll reconvene after the retest. :thumbsup:
